problem_text:
A logistics firm must coordinate a circuit for a specialized courier to collect sensitive documents from eight corporate offices.  
The offices are situated at the following grid positions (in miles):  

Office P: (56,66)  
Office Q: (149,198)  
Office R: (42,110)  
Office S: (49,91)  
Office T: (29,16)  
Office U: (179,7)  
Office V: (134,115)  
Office W: (192,173)  

Travel distances between offices (in miles) have been precomputed:  

P to R: 46.2  
P to S: 26.0  
P to T: 56.8  
P to U: 136.4  
P to V: 92.1  
P to W: 173.0  
Q to R: 138.5  
Q to S: 146.5  
Q to T: 218.0  
Q to U: 193.3  
Q to V: 84.3  
Q to W: 49.7  
R to S: 20.2  
R to T: 94.9  
R to U: 171.4  
R to V: 92.1  
R to W: 162.7  
S to T: 77.6  
S to U: 154.8  
S to V: 88.3  
S to W: 164.8  
T to U: 150.3  
T to V: 144.3  
T to W: 226.3  
U to V: 117.0  
U to W: 166.5  
V to W: 82.0  

Due to a regulatory restriction, there is no permitted direct route between Office P and Office Q.  
Moreover, for security reasons, exactly one of two specified corridors must be part of the itinerary: either the link between Office Q and Office R, or the link between Office R and Office S.  

The objective is to determine the minimal total travel distance for a closed loop that visits each office precisely once and returns to the origin office.
